# Vessantaracariya (Cp 9)

**ID:** Cp 9  
**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Vessantaracariya  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0512m.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0512m.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vessantaracariya* ("The Conduct of Vessantara", Cp 9 or Cp I.9) is the ninth narrative of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Bareau; Wood 2005; Matsumura 1980]. Rather than employing the standard narrative label *jātaka*, the collection frames its episodes as *cariya* ("conduct") to illustrate the Bodhisatta's perfection of specific virtues; the *Vessantaracariya* belongs to the opening set of ten narratives dedicated to the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) [Wood 2005]. Traditional poetic accounts associate King Vessantara's extreme generosity with the era of the past Buddha Kassapa [Jennings 1948], focusing on his readiness to renounce his children, wife, and wealth for the attainment of omniscience (*sabbaññuta*) [Bareau].

 Outside Pali, the Vessantara cycle constitutes one of the most famous Buddhist narratives, paralleled by the *Viśvantara Jātaka* in Āryaśūra's Sanskrit *Jātakamālā* and the *Viśvantarāvadāna* (no. 23) in Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* [Wood 2005; Matsumura 1980].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: Mil 5.1.4 Pathavicalanapañha; Mil 6.3.1 Vessantarapañha

**Sources**

- [Bareau] André Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka et les Jātaka Pāli — Documented the position of the text in the collection, its thematic verse on giving for omniscience, and references to B. C. Law's edition.
- [Wood 2005] Leela Aditi Wood, Buddha and the Shape of Belief: Indic Visual Jatakamalas, vol. 1 (2005) — Analyzed the genre distinction between cariya and jātaka, the text's place in the dānapāramitā section, and comparisons with Āryaśūra's Jātakamālā.
- [Matsumura 1980] Hisashi Matsumura, Four Avadānas from the Gilgit Manuscripts (1980) — Supplied cross-references to the Vessantarajātaka, Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā, and Barua's edition of the Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Jennings 1948] James George Jennings, The Vedantic Buddhism of the Buddha (1948) — Noted the traditional chronological placement of Vessantara's sacrifice during the era of Kassapa Buddha.
